findings: Inbound idempotency stores MAX message/chat IDs before Telegram send; delivery mapping adds Telegram IDs. This is event delivery identity, not file-byte or perceptual image equality.
Retry policy computes bounded exponential delay and message-age expiry; it provides no duplicate-file index or image matching contract.
Optional repository transaction helper yields without transaction when adapter lacks it; no runtime durability/bridge qualification performed.
Same message/attachment/kind upsert preserves first non-null destination and source, updates timestamp.
Different message ID creates distinct row even with all other values identical. No content digest in this SQL contract.
Duplicate key includes both message ID and chat ID; another chat does not match.
Upsert fills delivery IDs and retains them on later null update; direction changes while original created_at remains.

Media recovery cache keys chat/message/attachment index/kind, stores filename/dimensions/references and optional encrypted payload; no content digest or perceptual matching in this module. It is delivery recovery metadata, not file identity.

Payload lookup requires expires_at strictly greater than now; metadata entry lookup lacks expiry condition, while purge deletes expires_at<=now. These are distinct APIs; no incorrect caller use established.

Upsert overwrites metadata but COALESCE preserves prior encrypted payload when new encryption returns null; save returns whether new ciphertext exists, not whether old ciphertext is present. Static contract only, crypto/runtime not tested.
